label: Local Worker/D1 binding behavior (not memory conformance, not Node/SQLite, not remote production)

sharedConformance.driver: Node process; every storage call through Miniflare's D1 binding proxy into workerd's local D1

inWorkerConformance.driver: runner and adapter bundled into one Worker, executing inside workerd against env.DB; restart reopens handles only

results.proves: explicit schema initialization seeds only an absent site; a service write commits through one batch
stale CAS, duplicate revision id and duplicate (entry, sequence) each refuse the whole batch with no writes
with no head row every commit is refused and no record is orphaned; the changes() postcondition aborts a batch whose UPDATE matched zero rows
a real CHECK failure placed right after the head UPDATE aborts the batch; reported as HostedD1Error(failed), never revision-conflict
results.diagnostic: D1 rolled back the commit: D1_ERROR: CHECK constraint failed: json_valid(result): SQLITE_CONSTRAINT (extended: SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_CHECK)

results.proves: a response lost after the D1 batch completed recovers through its receipt exactly once; a different request under that key is refused
a D1 wait that times out reports an unknown outcome, the write still commits later and is recovered under the same key; a retry that wins first makes the late original refuse
results.diagnostic: D1 did not answer within 150 ms. The write may still commit; read the operation's receipt before retrying.

results.proves: a row over D1's 2,000,000-byte limit is refused before submission; atomicity is not weakened by splitting
stopping workerd with a batch in flight leaves head, receipt and revision all present or all absent after reopen

observed.acknowledgement: unacknowledged: D1 commit outcome is unknown: Cannot use disposed instance

results.proves: a new workerd process on the same directory reads the site, receipts and proposals without seeding; re-initialization is a no-op

initialization.driver: one real local D1 database per case; refusals compare complete before/after snapshots of schema objects, definitions and table rows

cases.proves: a database with no application objects is created and seeded in one batch
a valid populated store reopens without any write, before and after a workerd restart
an older marker table with no other tables is refused; no table is created

injectedFaults.receipt-persistence: a real D1 CHECK failure statement inserted directly after the head UPDATE in the same batch
injectedFaults.before-commit: the same failing statement appended as the last statement of the batch
injectedFaults.lost-acknowledgement: the batch completes durably, then the adapter discards the response and reports an unknown outcome
injectedFaults.hold: a commit is prepared and held before submission while another handle commits (interleaving)
injectedFaults.uncertain-timeout: the real batch is held in flight while the adapter's own timeout expires; it is then released and commits
injectedFaults.runtime-stop: workerd is disposed while a batch is in flight

notReproduced: Production network partitions, D1 primary failover, replica lag and Cloudflare-side resets are not reproducible in local workerd.
